prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] Income statement · fiscal quarters (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "USD millions" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Fiscal 2024" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Full year" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "USD millions" · longest unbreakable word 104px · one-line width 454px
  col 2: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 42px
  col 3: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 45px · one-line width 45px
  col 4: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q3" · longest unbreakable word 45px · one-line width 45px
  col 5: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q4" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 44px
  col 6: header "Full year" · longest unbreakable word 54px · one-line width 68px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 553px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 552px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 553px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare income statement line items across fiscal 2024 quarters and against the full-year total, in USD millions.","reading":"Readers scan row labels to find a line item, then read across to compare quarters and the full year; they can also scan down a quarter to compare line items. The long cost-of-revenue label will create a taller row that can absorb its own wrapping.","groups":["Columns 2–5 are equivalent quarterly measures and benefit from similar widths.","Column 6 is another monetary measure but represents the full year; its distinct header needs more space if it is to stay on one line.","Column 1 identifies each row and needs most of the flexible text space."],"keep_intact":["Quarterly and full-year numeric values","Quarter identifiers Q1–Q4","Individual words in row labels and headers"],"may_wrap":["The long cost-of-revenue label at word boundaries","Research and development at word boundaries","Full year between its two words","USD millions between its two words"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[217,63,66,66,65,75],"idea":"Give the row labels the most space while keeping every numeric value intact, allowing Full year to wrap."},{"name":"B","widths":[199,66,66,66,66,89],"idea":"Use equal quarter widths and keep Full year on one line, accepting more wrapping in row labels."},{"name":"C","widths":[210,63,66,66,65,82],"idea":"Split the flexible space between row labels and the full-year column, allowing its header to wrap while giving it more breathing room."}]}
